transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is that my eating has just gotten so off lately. Some days I barely get down a cup of coffee and maybe a granola bar before I head in for a shift at the clinic. It's funny, actually, because the coffee machine in the break room has been broken for like three weeks now. They keep saying maintenance is going to come look at it, but you know how that goes. Anyway, my scrubs have been hanging loose on me, like really baggy, even though I’m not trying to lose weight or anything. I used to buy the Dickies brand because they fit better, but lately even those are just swimming on me. I think they changed the fabric blend or something, they feel thinner now. But yeah, I just haven't been eating much at all.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, you know? Like the day is already completely ruined before I even put on my badge. Which reminds me, my badge reel actually snapped the other day. It was one of those retractable ones they gave out for Hospital Week last year, the ones with the little clinic logo on them? I had to go all the way down to HR to get a new one, and you wouldn't believe the line just to get a piece of plastic. The lady working the desk, Carol, she was telling me this whole long story about her grandson's little league game while I was just standing there waiting. Usually I don't mind Carol, she brings in donuts on Fridays and she's nice enough, but I just couldn't even pretend to care about baseball. I don't even like baseball. I used to watch football, but the refs are just terrible lately. But anyway, yeah, I just wake up feeling so heavy and empty before I even get out the door.
Have you noticed any changes like feeling unusually hot, your heart racing, or your hands trembling recently?

No, not really. I mean, my hands don't shake, and I haven't been sweating or anything like that. The clinic is always freezing anyway, they keep the AC cranked year-round. You'd think working in healthcare they'd know people get cold, but no, it's like a meat locker in there. I actually have to wear a long-sleeve shirt under my scrubs most days. I got this pack of thermal shirts from Target a while back—the Goodfellow brand, you know? They're pretty decent for the price, but the sleeves are just a little too long, so I have to roll them up at the wrists. And then they get bunched up under the scrub top, which is annoying when I'm trying to draw blood or take vitals. But yeah, no racing heart or anything like that.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired, constipated, or having dry skin or hair over the past few weeks?

No, I haven't really noticed any of that. I mean, I'm tired, but I think that's just because I'm not sleeping great and the days just drag. But my skin and hair seem normal, and no issues in the bathroom. Speaking of the bathroom, though, the plumbing on the second floor of the clinic has been a nightmare lately. They had to shut down the men's room near the break area on Tuesday because one of the pipes just completely backed up. The smell was awful, like sulfur and old mop water. They had this guy come in, Gary I think his name was, from some local plumbing company. He had this massive tool belt, like ridiculously heavy-looking, and he was telling me how hard it is to find good apprentices these days. He said kids just don't want to learn a trade anymore, which, I mean, I get it, it's hard work. My uncle was an electrician, and his knees were completely shot by the time he was fifty. He used to have to wear these thick knee pads just to get around the house. But yeah, no, I haven't had any constipation or dry skin or anything like that.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or wishing you weren't alive during this time?

I haven't... I haven't actually made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But I do catch myself just wishing I wouldn't wake up in the morning, you know? Like it would just be so much easier if I just disappeared. It's like that feeling when you're watching a movie and you just want to hit pause and walk away, except you can't. I was actually watching this documentary the other night, about deep sea divers? The guys who go down in those little bells to fix oil rigs and stuff. They have to live in these pressurized chambers for weeks at a time. I can't even imagine being stuck in a tiny tube with three other guys, eating freeze-dried food and watching the same DVDs over and over. One of the guys in the documentary was talking about how the pressure messes with your voice, makes you sound like a cartoon character. I tried doing that voice for my nephew once, inhaling helium from a balloon at his birthday party. He thought it was hilarious, but then I got really lightheaded and had to sit down on the patio furniture. It was one of those cheap plastic chairs and one of the legs bent under me. But yeah, I don't have a plan to do anything, I just... I just think it would be easier if I wasn't here.
Would you say these symptoms have made it hard for you to keep up with your usual work duties and daily responsibilities, or have you still been able to manage them despite feeling this way?

Yeah, it's... it's definitely been hard. I feel like I'm barely managing, honestly. I've started making these really stupid, avoidable mistakes at the clinic, and I keep needing my coworkers to repeat really simple requests. Like, my supervisor Brenda will ask me to restock the exam rooms, and I just blank on what she said. Brenda just got this new car, by the way, a Subaru Outback. It's that weird dark green color, looks kind of like a pine tree. She was telling me in the breakroom about how the dealership tried to upsell her on the undercoating, which is such a scam. My dad used to sell used cars back in the nineties, and he always told me the undercoating was just a trick to squeeze an extra five hundred bucks out of people. He worked at this lot right next to a diner that had the absolute best cherry pie. They served it with that really thick, dense vanilla bean ice cream. I haven't had pie like that in years. 

But, um... yeah, work is tough right now. And even outside of work, I'm just avoiding everything. I used to go to these local chess nights, and I'd do group photography walks on the weekends, but I've stopped going to all of it. I just don't trust myself to keep up with the games or, you know, act normal around the other people right now. I have a Nikon camera for those walks, and the strap on it is getting really frayed anyway. I was looking to order a new one off Amazon, but then you have to sift through all those fake reviews, and it's just exhausting trying to figure out what's actually a decent product. People get paid to write those five-star reviews now, it's a whole industry. So I haven't bought one. But yeah, I'm just really not keeping up with much of anything.
